# The SWMDK application

**639 pupils in 30 classrooms**, cluster sizes 5–29, responses on 1–5.

Two prespecified scales: **teacher** (Items 1–6) and **classmate**
(Items 8, 9, 10, 11, 13).

## The result

### Teacher scale

| | Respondent-weighted | Equal-cluster |
|---|---|---|
| H | **0.6199** | **0.6223** |
| 95 % CI | [0.5728, 0.6692] | [0.5743, 0.6698] |
| length | 0.0964 | 0.0956 |

### Classmate scale

| | Respondent-weighted | Equal-cluster |
|---|---|---|
| H | **0.5923** | **0.5829** |
| 95 % CI | [0.5431, 0.6408] | [0.5347, 0.6345] |
| length | 0.0978 | 0.0998 |

The targets differ by **+0.0024** on teacher and **−0.0094** on classmate —
in opposite directions. That is the informative-cluster-size effect showing up
as something other than noise, and it is why the paper reports both rather than
picking one.

## What the clustering costs

| Teacher scale | Length |
|---|---|
| raw two-stage HBB (uncalibrated) | 0.1327 |
| **calibrated HBB** | **0.0964** |
| two-level delta comparator | 0.1004 |
| iid respondent bootstrap (ignores clustering) | 0.0803 |

The iid interval is **20 % narrower** than the calibrated cluster-aware one.
That gap is the cost of taking the clustering seriously — an analyst who
ignores it reports more precision than the design supports.

The calibrated interval reaches 96.0 % (teacher) and 98.5 % (classmate) of the
delta comparator's length, so the gain is real but modest against a
well-specified analytic alternative.

## Computation

12 tasks × 99,999 draws = **1,199,988 draws**, **zero invalid**. The width
multiplier at G = 30 is 0.7261.

Exact knots: 2 on the teacher respondent-weighted lane, 0 on equal-cluster.
Those are diagnostic disclosures of the transport path, not error flags — and
they bear on [the archival defect](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-archival-defect),
where an exact zero is the handled case.

## Stability

Maximum split-half discrepancy **8.75e-4**, against an interval about 0.096
wide. Minimum category mass 0.0031, minimum category count 2.

## Independent reproduction

The oracle lane recomputes both scales from `data(SWMDK)` with the `mokken`
package and reproduces **Koopman et al. (2022)'s published values**:

| Scale | Published | Recomputed |
|---|---|---|
| teacher | 0.62 | 0.6199 |
| classmate | 0.592 | 0.5923 |

```bash
Rscript verification/oracles/run_oracles.R
```

This is the strongest external check in the package: a different implementation,
run on the same data, reproducing numbers published by different authors.
